m1_zero_omission_notes.chapter_executive_summary: Covers measures of central tendency for grouped data: Mean (Direct, Assumed Mean, Step-Deviation methods), Mode, and Median, along with the empirical relationship between them.

detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Direct Method: x̄ = Σ(fi * xi) / Σfi. Assumed Mean: x̄ = a + [Σ(fi * di) / Σfi] where di = xi - a. Step-Deviation: x̄ = a + [Σ(fi * ui) / Σfi] * h where ui = (xi - a)/h.

detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 13.2 Mode and Median of Grouped Data
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Mode = l + [(f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2)] * h. Median = l + [(n/2 - cf) / f] * h.

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: Midpoint of a class interval: (Upper Limit + Lower Limit) / 2.
The class interval with the highest frequency.
The class interval whose cumulative frequency is just greater than or equal to n/2.

level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.model_answer: Class mark xi = (15 + 35)/2 = 50/2 = 25. Class length h = 35 - 15 = 20.

level_4_competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A survey regarding heights (in cm) of 51 girls of Class X was conducted. Heights: <140 (4), <145 (11), <150 (29), <155 (40), <160 (46), <165 (51).

questions_and_answers.question: Find median height.
questions_and_answers.answer: Convert to continuous intervals. n=51 => n/2 = 25.5. Median class 145-150. Median = 145 + [(25.5 - 11)/18]*5 = 145 + (14.5/18)*5 = 149.03 cm.

m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.frequent_student_error: Using cumulative frequency cf of the modal/median class instead of the PRECEDING class in the median formula.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.root_cause: Misinterpreting cf term in median formula.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.correct_approach: The 'cf' in median formula ALWAYS refers to cumulative frequency of the class PRECEDING the median class.
